newsitem.title: USA: Rainy weather slows Kansas fieldwork.
newsitem.headline: Rainy weather slows Kansas fieldwork.

text.p: Successive rain showers over Kansas prevented farmers from completing much fieldwork during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said in its weekly crop progress report.
Fourteen percent of Kansas wheat acreage was seeded, ahead of 10 percent last year but lagging the 16-percent average.
Harvest of fall crops made little progress due to rain. Thirteen percent of corn was harvested, versus seven last year and the average of 24 percent.
Corn condition was rated 85 percent good to excellent, 12 fair and three poor to very poor.

Sorghum condition was rated 86 percent good to excellent, 13 percent fair and one percent poor. Eight percent of sorghum was harvested, versus one last year and the average of eight. Corn earworms continued to be a problem in sorghum fields.
Soybeans were rated 84 percent good to excellent, 14 fair and two percent poor. Two percent of the crop was harvested, versus one percent last year and the average of six percent.
Topsoil moisture was rated one percent short, 69 percent adequate and 30 percent surplus.
Pasture condition was rated 77 percent good to excellent, 19 percent fair and four percent poor.
